messages:
liam: Heads up — ap3a rack19 just had a cascade. One node lost power and now NVLink/interconnect fabric is flapping across 3/8 GPUs. Multiple jobs failing with InternalError: nvlink timeout. I'm pulling logs now.

ops-bot: Alert: GPU node gpu-node-19 in ap3a-rack19 reported link down (NVLINK). Incident INC-1854002468 created.

sanjay: quick question: is this host-level kernel OOPS or purely NV fabric? can someone paste dmesg + nvidia-smi output?

liam: quick snippets — `kubectl describe node gpu-node-19` shows NotReady, reason: Kernel OOM? Kernel log excerpt: ```[12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, 0000(0x00000000): GPU reported multiple Xid errors``` also seeing `nvlink: link down` messages.

katie: I'll start draining affected nodes. Command I'm running: `fleetctl tag set gpu-node-19 state=draining` then `kubectl drain gpu-node-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. We'll drain the 3 with obvious errors first.

emma: Routing note: hosted API fallback to eu-west is enabled but pool is constrained. Suggest shifting low-priority and non-prod inference first. Maria, can you approve cross-region burst to eu-west reserved pool?

maria: approved up to 20% burst into eu-west reserved pool for non-prod/low-priority. Watch for cost; prefer spot where possible.

liam: caveat — some model builds on ap3a are pinned to a quantized/optimized binary that eu-west doesn't have. That will increase latency and may change outputs. Ops, can we add a model-compat fallback that sends requests to a compatible variant?

sanjay: plan: canary shift 5% traffic for 15m, monitor p50/p95 latency and error_rate. If error_rate > 3% revert. I'll configure rollout via traffic-manager.

katie: hardware update from tech: PSU on gpu-node-19 failed and we're seeing intermittent PCIe/NVLink link errors between node-19/20/21. Could be riser or switch port. I'll open a ticket with datacenter ops.

maria: ordering parts: 1x PSU, 1x PCIe riser for rack19. ETA for onsite swap ~4h. Continue draining and keep spare capacity at 10%.

liam: commands I executed: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-19 && kubectl drain gpu-node-19 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data``` pods rescheduled properly — logs attached in the incident tool (snip).

ops-bot: Evacuation update: 3 nodes drained, 12 pods rescheduled to other racks. Autoscaler triggered +2 jobs to fill capacity.

emma: cost note: shifting 20% non-prod to eu-west estimated +$1.2k/day. Recommend enabling more aggressive batching/caching for the affected routes while in failover to reduce token spend.

maria: incident owners set: @sanjay (incident owner), @katie (hardware owner), @emma (cost/traffic owner). Next update in 15 minutes.

liam: added a check — vendor flagged older NVLink firmware on the affected nodes. After hardware swap we'll schedule firmware update on standby nodes, staged in canary to avoid mass restarts.

katie: RMA flow started. I'll update ETA once tech confirms onsite.

maria: thanks team. @oncall-rotations-bot please notify tomorrow's primary oncall to follow burn-in and replacement verification.

oncall-rotations-bot: Noted. Primary oncall @alex will be paged at 08:00 UTC for handoff.

liam: ACTIONS SUMMARY: 1) drained 3 nodes (katie) 2) canary shift 5% (sanjay) 3) cross-region burst approved up to 20% non-prod (maria/emma) 4) parts ordered & RMA (katie) 5) firmware plan after replacement (liam). Next update in 15m.
